record.text: The teletext feature is outmoded and should not be considered in the new project design.
Financial objectives are unclear or missing with no consensus on a revenue target, and there is pricing risk as the proposed price point may not align with market expectations or willingness to pay.
PM MIO086 will coordinate with Intel or IBM to obtain technical backup for speech recognition and related design work.
The remote control should be used only for the TV.

There are usability and speech recognition challenges: 35% say speech recognition is too difficult to use; 50% say they can't find the remote half the time; ambient noise and on-screen dialogue can cause misinterpretation of commands requiring robust filtering; training for voice commands may be time-consuming for users; speech recognition could impact battery life, necessitating wireless charging or solar cells; and there is uncertainty whether speech recognition should rely on one-word commands or allow longer phrases.
PM MIO086 will help Christine identify and contact technical companies to assist in slimming the design.
ID(FIE073) will work on the components concept.

No final decision on which features to include has been reached; the group is debating whether to start with all features or prune later, and remote UI issues include too many buttons and unclear labels along with concerns about findability and search capability; time pressure ended the discussion with important decisions unresolved.
The group proposed setting a target to achieve at least 50 million Euro in revenue, and noted that there is currently no explicit financial objective or consensus on the revenue target.
The management said they want something new and do not want to continue with certain existing facilities.

gold.text: Management required a television-only remote without teletext that conveys the corporate image.
The industrial designer presented requirements and design preferences, including reliable power control, finding the remote, appearance and materials.
The team discussed durability and casing materials such as plastic and titanium, without settling a material or resolving the cost tradeoff.

The marketing expert reported a nominal EUR 25 sale price and EUR 12.50 production allowance, and survey interest in speech recognition, a locator and easier use; he warned that the proposed features would strain that cost allowance.
The project manager offered to recommend technical companies and coordinate information on speech recognition if the industrial designer requested specific help.
Participants wanted clearer management guidance on the tradeoff between a simple affordable remote and an innovative, more expensive one.
The user interface designer emphasized few, clear buttons, prominent frequently used controls, and a sleek, simple design.
The user interface designer asked the team to select features before investing effort. Time ran out, and the group deferred further discussion until after the meeting and a later meeting.
The closing assignments were a components concept for the industrial designer, an interface concept for the user interface designer, and continued trendwatching for marketing.
The industrial designer will develop the components concept for the next design phase.
The user interface designer will develop the user interface concept for the next design phase.
The marketing expert will continue trendwatching to inform the marketing concept.
The project manager offered to recommend companies such as Intel or IBM and coordinate speech-recognition information if the industrial designer requested help.

Final feature selection was deferred. The industrial designer suggested starting with all features, the user interface designer objected to wasted design effort, and further discussion was left until after the meeting.
A slim shape, simple interface, locator, voice recognition and durable casing were favored design ideas, with feasibility, cost and final feature selection still unresolved.
The team did not resolve whether to design all suggested features first or prune them before developing the concept; discussion was deferred when meeting time ran out.
The desired price/feature tradeoff and management's willingness to fund a more innovative product remained unclear.
The project manager will send the meeting minutes to the participants.
The project manager will email the project aim and financial-goal information after the team could not locate the earlier project-plan/budget file.
